subject: physical-education
title: Investigation or close reading: ready position
essentialQuestion: How can understanding net and wall activities help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?

lessonFamilyPlan.instructionalPurpose: read supplied information and choose a safe tactical response
lessonFamilyPlan.guidedEmphasis: Name two available options, one constraint, and the cue that makes one option stronger.
lessonFamilyPlan.independentEvidence: Solve a fresh arrangement without answer-bearing coaching and explain the choice.
lessonFamilyPlan.evidencePurpose: decision quality, tactical reasoning, planning, and reflection

goal: I can read supplied information and choose a safe tactical response for ready position, using a safe standard or equal-credit adapted route, and explain the cue or decision that shows success.
successOverview: Success is safe setup, use of the taught Scan, choose, act, recover. cue or decision, a fresh bounded application, and a short explanation. Credit never depends on body position, speed, athletic talent, comparison, or use of the standard route.
readinessCheck: Choose between two supplied position options and explain one reason.
Choose movement, seated, supported, mobility-aid, low-space, no-equipment, or described evidence without explaining why.
Use the complete described route if guardian permission, safe space, equipment, movement, a partner, or a real setting is unavailable.
materials: Optional: three soft household markers or a paper diagram.
Use fingers, drawn points, or imaginary positions.
movementCues: SCAN the whole supplied space or diagram.
CHOOSE the open or protective option before moving.
ACT with a controlled point, gesture, step, or wheel path.
RECOVER to protect the next likely option.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Rehearse the model slowly, change one variable, and explain the cue or decision before adding complexity.

movementModel.title: Model for ready position
movementModel.startingPosition: Use three paper marks, objects, or imagined points for self, target, and open space.
movementModel.action: Scan the arrangement, choose one option, show the path with a point or controlled movement, and recover to a useful position.
movementModel.commonError: Following the object or first option without checking open space and the next play.
movementModel.correction: Freeze the diagram, name two options, choose one reason, and mark the recovery point before moving.
movementModel.notice: Notice information and decision quality rather than opponent outcome or speed.
movementModel.adaptedModel: Use the seated, supported, mobility-aid, reduced-range, object-modeled, or described route and preserve this evidence: Notice information and decision quality rather than opponent outcome or speed.
movementModel.safetyBoundary: Use solo diagram, shadow, or walk-through practice; tactical evidence never requires guarding contact, wrestling, tackling, or collision. No contact, collision, real opponent, scored contest, or movement toward another person.

guidedPractice.prompt: Name two available options, one constraint, and the cue that makes one option stronger. Choose between two supplied position options and explain one reason. Apply it to ready position.
guidedPractice.support: Use the model cue: Scan, choose, act, recover.
guidedPractice.feedback: If the target is unclear, return to the starting position and use this correction: Freeze the diagram, name two options, choose one reason, and mark the recovery point before moving.

guidedPractice.prompt: Show one open-space or protective-position decision on a fixed diagram.
guidedPractice.support: Watch for this contrast: Following the object or first option without checking open space and the next play.
guidedPractice.feedback: Keep the safe version when the learner can show or explain notice information and decision quality rather than opponent outcome or speed.

practiceProgression.name: Entry version
practiceProgression.task: Name two available options, one constraint, and the cue that makes one option stronger. Show one open-space or protective-position decision on a fixed diagram.
practiceProgression.successCheck: Show or explain the target for ready position once with the safe boundary intact.
practiceProgression.changedVariable: None; begin with the simplest safe version.
practiceProgression.learnerChoice: Remain here, reduce range or pace, add support, rest, or switch to the described route.
practiceProgression.maximumBoundary: No contact, collision, real opponent, scored contest, or movement toward another person.

practiceProgression.name: One change
practiceProgression.task: Show one open-space or protective-position decision on a fixed diagram. Then change only one target, boundary, defender marker, teammate marker, or rule. Keep the decision quality, tactical reasoning, planning, and reflection purpose visible.
practiceProgression.successCheck: Name what changed and keep the same cue, control, decision, and safety boundary.
practiceProgression.changedVariable: Change only one target, boundary, defender marker, teammate marker, or rule.
practiceProgression.learnerChoice: Progress only by choice; repeat or regress whenever the cue or control is not clear.
practiceProgression.maximumBoundary: No contact, collision, real opponent, scored contest, or movement toward another person.

practiceProgression.name: Fresh application
practiceProgression.task: Solve a fresh arrangement without answer-bearing coaching and explain the choice. Solve a fresh arrangement by naming the information, choice, action path, and recovery position.
practiceProgression.successCheck: Complete the fresh bounded application and identify the cue or decision that controlled it.
practiceProgression.changedVariable: The learner selects a new safe example, arrangement, or condition.
practiceProgression.learnerChoice: Use any standard or equal-credit route, take breaks, or finish through description without penalty.
practiceProgression.maximumBoundary: No contact, collision, real opponent, scored contest, or movement toward another person.

independentActivity.title: Fresh application: ready position
directions: Solve a fresh arrangement by naming the information, choice, action path, and recovery position.
Use this cue or decision: Scan, choose, act, recover.
Provide the selected evidence without a recording or body metric.
independentActivity.freshTask: Solve a fresh arrangement without answer-bearing coaching and explain the choice. Solve a fresh arrangement by naming the information, choice, action path, and recovery position.
independentActivity.independenceBoundary: A trusted human or future Tutor may read directions, define a cue, and offer an approved route. They may not perform the decision for the learner, claim unapproved observation, certify physical completion, or provide medical or return clearance.

warmUp: Point to open and protected space in a simple three-point model.
Rehearse one controlled move-and-recover path without an opponent.
coolDown: Return to the easiest comfortable version or rest.
Restore optional equipment and space safely.
Name one cue, safety choice, or next adjustment without reporting body data.

spaceSetup: Use one tabletop or one arm-span of clear floor. Real opponent, contact, court, scored contest, or group play is not required. Low-space access remains available before and during the lesson. Cleanup: return optional items only after movement has stopped and the path is clear.

optional: Optional: three soft household markers or a paper diagram.
householdSubstitutes: Use fingers, drawn points, or imaginary positions.
prohibited: No contact, collision, real opponent, scored contest, or movement toward another person.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit solo route: point, gesture, draw, or describe ready position, open space, one decision, and recovery; no opponent or group is required.

safetyRules: Check the surface, ceiling, boundary, people, pets, cords, breakables, footwear or mobility supports, and any optional item before movement.
Use solo diagram, shadow, or walk-through practice; tactical evidence never requires guarding contact, wrestling, tackling, or collision.
Use learner-selected range, pace, and demand. Control, decisions, and understanding matter more than force, distance, duration, or repetitions.
If the environment cannot be made safe, do not perform movement; use the equal-credit described route or stop and tell a trusted adult.
stoppingRules: REST / ADJUST: You may pause, rest, reduce pace or range, use support, switch to an approved route, or finish for the day at any time. You may resume only when comfortable and the environment is safe. Rest and adaptation never reduce credit.

STOP AND TELL: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, an injury concern, damaged equipment, or an unsafe environment. Tell a trusted adult and do not continue to test the concern.

DO NOT RESUME: After a head impact, an injury concern, or a symptom that persists or worsens, remain out until the authorized guardian or qualified professional says it is safe. A learner, browser, or Tutor cannot provide clearance.

adaptationRoutes.seated: Use a stable seated position and preserve the Scan, choose, act, recover. evidence through upper-body movement, pointing, gesture, object modeling, or description.
adaptationRoutes.supported: Place an approved stable support before beginning and use it through the whole attempt; score the cue or decision for ready position, not unsupported balance.
adaptationRoutes.reducedRange: Use the smallest comfortable movement, eye-gaze choice, point, or gesture that still shows the target cue or decision for ready position.
adaptationRoutes.reducedPaceOrDemand: Complete one stage at a time with learner-chosen breaks, remain at the entry version, or split the lesson across short sittings.
adaptationRoutes.mobilityAidCompatible: Keep the mobility aid positioned and used as approved; adapt the path around the aid and score the same Scan, choose, act, recover. evidence.
adaptationRoutes.solo: Use the supplied solo, shadow, diagram, imagined-role, or fictional-situation route; no partner, opponent, group, or audience is required.
adaptationRoutes.lowSpace: Use the one-arm-span or one-seat setup: Equal-credit solo route: point, gesture, draw, or describe ready position, open space, one decision, and recovery; no opponent or group is required.
adaptationRoutes.noEquipment: Equal-credit solo route: point, gesture, draw, or describe ready position, open space, one decision, and recovery; no opponent or group is required.
adaptationRoutes.describedOrDecisionRoute: Describe, draw, gesture, point, sign, or model Solve a fresh arrangement by naming the information, choice, action path, and recovery position. This is a complete equal-credit route when movement is not appropriate.

accessibleAdaptation: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice information and decision quality rather than opponent outcome or speed. The standard route is never required and adaptation never lowers credit.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit solo route: point, gesture, draw, or describe ready position, open space, one decision, and recovery; no opponent or group is required.
activitySteps: Choose a standard or equal-credit response route.
Read the STOP AND TELL rule.
Complete the warm-up when it applies.
Use the safe finish when it applies.
Answer the short reflection or leave it blank.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Following the object or first option without checking open space and the next play.

learnerEvidence: One guided response using Scan, choose, act, recover..
One fresh bounded application or complete described equivalent for ready position.
One cue, decision, safety, or next-step explanation.
evidenceExpectations.observer: A learner may self-check a cue and a trusted human may review the selected evidence. A Tutor, browser, camera, wearable, or self-report cannot certify physical completion, guardian permission, or safe return.
doNotCollect: weight, appearance, body composition, calories, body shape, fitness norms, speed versus peers, or athletic talent
diagnosis, disability reason, symptom history, or private medical information
photo, video, audio, wearable data, location proof, or exercise log

retryPlan.trigger: Retry when the evidence does not yet show the target cue or decision for ready position; name the missing observable part without judging the learner.
retryPlan.simplerSetup: Choose between two supplied position options and explain one reason.
retryPlan.differentCue: Replace the full cue set with: “Scan, choose, act, recover.”
retryPlan.alternateModel: Contrast this common error — Following the object or first option without checking open space and the next play. — with this correction — Freeze the diagram, name two options, choose one reason, and mark the recovery point before moving.
retryPlan.boundedPractice: Show one open-space or protective-position decision on a fixed diagram.
retryPlan.freshRetry: Solve a fresh arrangement by naming the information, choice, action path, and recovery position. Use a new safe example rather than repeating the scored attempt.
retryPlan.exitCriterion: Return to independent work when the fresh retry shows or explains notice information and decision quality rather than opponent outcome or speed. A safety stop, rest, or adaptation is never recorded as failure.

guardianAuthority.when: Guardian permission is required before real movement, optional equipment, a real location, partner, outdoor route, or progression is used.
guardianAuthority.requiredAction: The guardian confirms that the bounded space, optional equipment, and activity route are permitted before movement.
guardianAuthority.minimumRecord: Record only permission status or that the equal-credit described route was used; collect no body, health, media, location, or performance data.
guardianAuthority.confirmationBoundary: Guardian confirmation may establish permission or occurrence only. It does not certify academic mastery, physical quality, diagnosis, effort, body status, or safe return.
guardianAuthority.equalCreditAlternative: When guardian review, real movement, equipment, space, partner, or location is unavailable, the supplied solo described/decision route is the complete equal-credit lesson.

may: offer an approved presentation or activity route
coach how the learner presents their own evidence
route to rest, stop, retry, or adult handoff
mustNot: cannot diagnose, prescribe, rehabilitate, or give medical clearance
cannot claim unapproved observation or certify physical completion
cannot override rest, stop, adaptation, guardian authority, professional authority, or safe return
cannot choose the answer or action for fresh independent evidence
cannot score body data, norms, appearance, talent, or peer comparison

keyPoints: Use three paper marks, objects, or imagined points for self, target, and open space.
Scan the arrangement, choose one option, show the path with a point or controlled movement, and recover to a useful position.
Freeze the diagram, name two options, choose one reason, and mark the recovery point before moving.
privacySafeScenario: Use a supplied or invented non-personal example of ready position; do not disclose private health information or recreate a hazard.
studentTask: Solve a fresh arrangement without answer-bearing coaching and explain the choice. Solve a fresh arrangement by naming the information, choice, action path, and recovery position. Use any approved standard or equal-credit route. Name the cue or decision that controlled the result; no body metric, comparison, recording, or physical-completion claim is required.
knowledgeCheck: State the starting position, action, key cue, common error, and correction for ready position. Then distinguish optional REST / ADJUST from STOP AND TELL and DO NOT RESUME.
completionCriteria: The learner uses a safe setup or accurately describes it for ready position.
The learner applies Scan, choose, act, recover. in one guided attempt and one fresh application or complete described equivalent.
The learner distinguishes learner-controlled rest from STOP AND TELL and DO NOT RESUME conditions.
Any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route earns equal credit for the same cue or decision evidence.
adaptationChoices: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice information and decision quality rather than opponent outcome or speed. The standard route is never required and adaptation never lowers credit.
extensionChallenge: Apply ready position under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.

optionalReflection.prompt: Which cue, decision, safety check, or adaptation preserved the target for ready position, and what would you keep or change in a next safe attempt?

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires maximal effort, exercise as punishment, or movement through pain.
This task never requires gym access, specialized equipment, or a purchase; the no-equipment path earns equal credit.
